text:
A: Hiya, erm, sorry, is it working? I think it's working.
B: Yeah, I can see you.
A: Oh good, sorry. I'm Holly. Is it, erm, do we just chat?
B: Think so. I'm Tracey. Dagenham.
A: Oh, hiya. I'm in Stockport. So, erm, what do you do? Sorry, is that a boring question?
B: No, it's fine. Office cleaning, evenings. In Romford.
A: Oh, right. Are you going in after this, then?
B: Yeah, five o'clock. Then I'm knackered by nine, d'you know what I mean.
A: Yeah. I'm an apprentice lab technician, so, like, testing samples and that. Full time, and college every other week. I'm absolutely shattered most days and I'm only eighteen, so I don't know what I'll be like later, haha.
B: Eighteen. Blimey.
A: I know, sorry. Everyone says that.
B: No, I didn't mean nothing by it. Just young. Lab, though, that's clever. You must be good at all that.
A: Erm, kind of? I'm alright at the actual lab bits, I'm just rubbish at the paperwork. I keep doing my portfolio the night before. Do you know what I mean?
B: I hate paperwork. They make you do these online things at work, chemicals and lifting and that. I just click through them.
A: Haha, don't tell anyone.
B: Who's gonna know?
A: Fair. Oh, sorry, my dog's snoring, can you hear that?
B: Is that a dog? What've you got?
A: She's a Staffy cross, Bonnie. She's dead old now, she just sleeps on my bed all day.
B: I've got a Staffy. Duchess. She's old as well, her back legs have gone dodgy. Vet wants a fortune, so we just sort of manage.
A: Aw, no. Does she still go for walks?
B: Round Parsloes Park, slow. Takes forever. People think I'm dragging her, but she stops every two foot to sniff something, and I'm stood there like a lemon.
A: Bonnie does that! I walk her after tea every night, and it's like half an hour to do one lap. My mum says she's milking it.
B: They know, though, don't they? Duchess knows exactly what she's doing.
A: Yeah, she does. I honestly don't know what I'll do when she goes. Sorry, that's a bit grim.
B: No, I know. I think about it with Duchess. We ain't got kids, so, d'you know what I mean, she's sort of it.
A: Yeah. Aw.
B: Anyway. That puzzle thing, you was doing that alone as well, yeah?
A: Yeah! I was so stressed, I felt like I was getting it all wrong. Was there a right answer?
B: Dunno. I thought they'd be watching to see if you was thick or something.
A: Same. I kept going back and changing them.
B: I just put anything. Is that alright, d'you reckon?
A: I'm sure it's fine. I don't think they're...
